name: Vai Siʻi
reason: Rule 1: no visitor source names it; only Wikipedia. Re-looked on Pocket Guide pages, nothing.
objection: Real crater lake, but it is part of the Niuafoʻou caldera and Vai Lahi, with no way to visit it independently.

name: Niuafoʻou Caldera
reason: Rule 3: part of a larger place; the caldera is where Vai Lahi sits and the island is listed, megapode viewing is an activity not a place.
objection: Two counted sources and the megapode is a genuine draw for birders; but no defined spot, and it duplicates Vai Lahi/island.

name: Futu Wharf
reason: Rule 2/3: a landing pier, a gateway not a draw; one source mentions it only as the way in.
objection: Only landing place on the island, so every visitor passes it.

name: Niuafoʻou Lava Fields
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage mentions it only in background text; Pocket Guide has no entry (re-checked). No defined place to visit.
objection: 1929-46 lava flows are the island's signature story and are visible everywhere.

name: Mokotu
reason: Rule 1: only the island Wikipedia article names it; no visitor source.
objection: Crater-rim high point, but nobody directs visitors there.

name: Hihifo Spring
reason: Rules 1-2: two counted sources (Pocket Guide #1 thing to do on Niuatoputapu, opened); freshwater spring with steps for a dip.
objection: Against: a small village pool also used by locals, probably 15-30 minutes, modesty expectations, tiny island few will reach. For: named by two sources as the island's top activity.

name: Niuatoputapu Highest Point
reason: Rules 1-2: two counted sources (opened); guided 157 m climb with views over the island and Tafahi, a real activity.
objection: Against: unnamed hill, needs a local guide, not a defined trailhead. For: a half-day walk a guide promotes and has a viewpoint.

name: Niuatoputapu Reefs
reason: Rule 3: not a specific place; diving/snorkelling across the whole outer reef with no operators or rentals.
objection: Two counted sources praise the unspoiled reef; but it is an activity across the island, not a sited spot.

name: Niuatoputapu Shipwreck
reason: Rule 1/3: unnamed wreck on an outer reef, one source, local must show the way; no stable identity.
objection: Dive wrecks are real draws; but unnameable and unsited.

name: Falehau Wharf
reason: Rule 2/3: a wharf where boats leave for Tafahi; the place it goes to (Tafahi) is the spot.
objection: Practical gateway for the Tafahi trip.

name: Hihifo
reason: Rule 2/3: a village; the draws in it (spring) are covered separately, nothing else to see; offices and post office are not attractions.
objection: Largest village of the Niuas, base for visitors.

name: Vaipoa
reason: Rule 2/4: village; Sunday service is a recurring event and not a place; the boat departure is covered by Tafahi.
objection: Two counted sources name it, with an open church service.

name: Falehau
reason: Rule 2/4: village with a harbour; Sunday church service is an event, boats for Tafahi are covered by Tafahi.
objection: Two counted sources; harbour village that guides single out.
